title: PRD: Convert postmortem action items into verifiable degradation and fallback requirements
creator: Priya Nambiar
background: Recent production incidents exposed gaps between the incident runbook actions and the PRD-level acceptance criteria. Multiple postmortem action items described operator steps, but the product spec lacks deterministic verification steps to ensure those actions produce the expected customer-facing degradation behavior. This ticket captures the PRD changes to translate postmortem actions into measurable requirements, test harnesses, and rollout gates.
goal: Ensure every postmortem action that alters runtime or operational behavior is represented in the PRD as (a) an implementable requirement, (b) automated/verifiable acceptance tests, and (c) rollout gating criteria tied to SLOs and error budgets.
scope_changes: Add a new verification harness requirement (synthetic and traffic-shepherded) for fallback and degradation scenarios.
Mandate explicit runbook-to-PRD mapping for any incident action that changes default routing, cache priming, or autoscale policies.
Include acceptance gates for canary rollouts that exercise degraded paths (model fallback, regional failover, dedicated->hosted fallback).
Add metrics, dashboards, and alert thresholds that must be present before rollout (tail latency, 95th token latency, fallback rate, error-rate delta).
Define rollback criteria tied to customer-impacting SLO breaches and verified regression signals from the harness.
requirements: Every postmortem action item tagged as "operational" or "runtime" must list the corresponding PRD requirement id and owner.
Require an automated synthetic test that simulates the incident trigger (e.g., KV cache stall, cold start surge) and verifies fallback behavior within the target SLO window.
Define a deterministic test dataset and traffic profile for each regression class (coldstarts, KV cache regen, quantization fallback, regional outage) and store artifacts in the verification repo.
Add a configuration schema for 'fallback contracts' describing acceptable latency and token-quality deltas per customer tier.
Rollout gating: canary runs must show zero more-than-2x increase in tail latency and fallback rate below defined thresholds for 30 minutes under synthetic load before broader rollout.
Instrumentation: expose a per-request tag when a fallback path is used; telemetry must be queryable in console within 10 minutes of ingestion.
Include a test that validates operator runbook steps (e.g., cache regen, manual scaling) succeed in an isolated canary environment and produce the documented system state transitions.
acceptance_criteria: A verification harness repo and CI job exist that runs synthetic incident scenarios and produces a pass/fail report stored with the release artifact.
At least three incident-derived scenarios (KV cache stall, coldstart surge, cross-region flapping) are implemented in the harness with documented input profiles and expected outputs.
Console dashboard pages include new panels for 'fallback rate', 'fallback latency delta', and 'fallback attribution (model/region/autoscale)'.
Canary gating rules are defined in the PRD and implemented as a checklist in the release runbook; tooling prevents promotion unless gates are green or an approved exception is recorded.
Post-release smoke: automated regression checks run for 24h and report to the incident channel; a failing regression triggers immediate rollback per PRD policy.
Owners for each new requirement are assigned and listed in the PRD with SLAs for fixes and follow-ups.
milestones: 2026-03-15: PRD draft updated with mapping table from last three postmortems
2026-03-22: Engineering and SRE alignment workshop to review harness design
2026-03-29: Prototype synthetic scenarios implemented and first CI pipeline validated
2026-04-05: Finalize PRD additions and gating checklist; mark for runtime-1.20 scope
2026-04-12: Canary run and verification for runtime-1.20 pre-merge
risks: Building exhaustive synthetic scenarios is expensive and may not cover novel failure modes; mitigated by prioritizing highest-impact incidents first.
False positives in the harness could block releases; require an operator debug pathway and a documented exception process.
Telemetry latency may delay verification feedback; require 10-minute ingestion SLA from instrumentation team or degrade sensitivity.
Additional gating may slow delivery velocity; include time-boxed opt-in for low-risk minor releases.
decisions: Adopt a minimum-first approach: implement harness for top-3 incident classes identified in postmortems before broadening coverage.
Use traffic-shepherded synthetic tests rather than live-customer chaos for verification to avoid customer risk.
Represent fallback contracts as JSON schema embedded in the PRD and as a machine-readable artifact used by the canary tooling.
open_questions: Who owns the long-term maintenance of the verification harness? (Options: SRE, Runtime QA, or Shared team)
What signals constitute 'quality regression' for generator output when falling back to a smaller/quantized model?
Should fallback attribution be surfaced per-tenant in the console or only aggregated at the org level?
next_steps: Create PRD section 'Incident-to-Requirement mapping' and populate table with last 3 postmortems (owner: Priya).
Schedule a 90-minute alignment session with SRE and Runtime leads to finalize synthetic test design (owner: Ethan).
Spin up a verification repo and CI job skeleton; prototype KV cache stall scenario (owner: Runtime QA).
Draft canary checklist automation tickets for infra and console teams (owner: Release Eng).
notes: This PRD update is deliberately scoped to add verifiable acceptance criteria and tooling hooks; implementation tasks will be split into engineering tickets after PM/SRE/Runtime alignment. The goal is to turn tacit runbook knowledge into testable code and release gates.
operator_visible_changes: New console panels and a per-release verification report linked in the release notes. Operators will have a 'run harness' button for on-demand verification in staging.
